questions.q: Can this go passive? 'The sun rises in the east.'
questions.a: No — 'rises' is intransitive; nothing receives the action. A wrong answer 'The east is risen by the sun' shows the student moves words without checking transitivity.

questions.q: Better active or passive: 'The storm destroyed the crops.'
questions.a: Either works, but passive 'The crops were destroyed' is better when the damage is the news — the storm is already known. The defensible answer matters more than the choice.
'Happen' is intransitive — no object exists to promote to subject, so there is no legal passive. A wrong answer accepting it shows the transitivity check was skipped.

questions.q: Some verbs cannot go passive and some sentences should not: ______ verbs (sleep, arrive, happen) have no object to promote — 'The baby was slept' is impossible.
Fill in the blank: Some verbs cannot go passive and some sentences should not: ______ verbs (sleep, arrive, happen) have no object to promote — 'The baby was slept' is impossible.
Fill in the blank: ______ first: 'The accident happened' cannot invert — there is no object to move; 'was happened' is a classic wrong build.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student refuses passive for intransitive verbs, identifies when passive is the better choice (result-focus, unknown doer, formal/scientific register), and defends keeping active when the doer is the point.
